name: MacPGP
summary: Manage OpenPGP keys and encrypt, decrypt, sign or verify files and messages.
intro: MacPGP brings OpenPGP workflows to a native Mac interface. Finder and sharing extensions provide entry points for working with supported encrypted files.

features.title: Keys and recipients
features.body: Generate, import, export and delete OpenPGP keys.

features.title: Files and messages
features.body: Encrypt for recipients, decrypt supported content and work with signatures.

features.title: Finder integration
features.body: Use context actions, encrypted-file thumbnails and metadata-only Quick Look previews.

features.title: Keyserver tools
features.body: Search for, retrieve and publish public keys through configured keyservers.

support.title: Check compatibility
paragraphs: Use an Apple Silicon Mac running macOS 26.2 or later. Intel Macs are not supported by the current bridge.

support.title: Encryption and decryption
paragraphs: Import the intended recipient public key and verify its fingerprint. Decryption requires the matching private key and any required passphrase.

support.title: Enable extensions
paragraphs: Enable the relevant Finder, Quick Look, thumbnail or sharing extension in macOS settings. Relaunch Finder if changes are not reflected.

support.title: Keyserver failures
paragraphs: Check the selected server and network connection. Insecure search or retrieval requires explicit opt-in; uploads require secure transport.

support.title: Key deletion warnings
paragraphs: If deletion reports cleanup failures, retry the indicated cleanup. Keep any required private-key backup before deleting a key.

privacy.title: Local keys and files
paragraphs: Keyrings and preferences are stored locally. Encryption, decryption and signature operations process the selected content on the Mac; exported and decrypted files remain in their chosen locations.

privacy.title: Passphrases
paragraphs: Supported workflows can save passphrases in macOS Keychain. Temporary session clearing does not delete persisted Keychain items or secret keys.

privacy.title: Keyservers
paragraphs: Search and retrieval send queries or key identifiers to the chosen server. Publishing sends public-key material, which can include identity names and email addresses; deleting a local key does not retract published copies.

privacy.title: Extensions
paragraphs: A local shared container supplies public-key information to extensions. Quick Look displays metadata rather than decrypting file contents in the preview.

privacy.title: Deletion and diagnostics
paragraphs: Key deletion removes the key and attempts related metadata and passphrase cleanup, reporting failures. Files, backups and published key copies need separate handling. No integrated analytics or crash-reporting service was found in the inspected source.
